## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The change in `app/report.py:5` correctly rejects any header other than `REPORT v1`, but one of the two new tests should be fixed: `test_rejects_legacy_header` passes without ever reaching the version check. Regression protection for the new check comes only from `test_rejects_unsupported_header_with_complete_report`. This review found no correctness or silent-failure defects in the changed code.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- tests/test_report.py:11 — tests — `test_rejects_legacy_header` builds the input `"REPORT v1\nversion=v0"`, so its header is still `REPORT v1`, and the test can't fail if the version check breaks. `rsplit("v1", 1)` replaces only the last `v1`, which is in the body line `version=v1`, not in the header. The fixture also has no `END` line, so `parse_report` returns `None` at `app/report.py:3-4` before it reaches the header check at line 5. The comment at line 9 ("changing the fixture's version to v0") describes the intended input, not the actual one. To fix it, use a literal complete report with a legacy header, for example `"REPORT v0\nvalue=ok\nEND"`, or delete the test, since `test_rejects_unsupported_header_with_complete_report` already covers that input. — Maintainers reading the test name and comment will believe there are two guards for the legacy-header rejection when there is only one. If someone later reverts the check to `startswith("REPORT ")`, this test still passes.

## Suggestions
(none)

## Strengths
- `test_rejects_unsupported_header_with_complete_report` (tests/test_report.py:15-17) uses a report that passes the `END` and length checks, so it isolates the new header check. Under the old `startswith("REPORT ")` logic it would fail.
